title: No hymns; the German band prank in Algiers
summary: Mello says they played no hymns because of their large repertoire, then tells how he and others played German band music at a parade in Algiers, angering Laine.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Did they ever use any hymns in any of these jazz tunes? Any who? Hymns. You know, religious tunes. No, no, no. You know, they do that now. You hear them take these spirals. Yeah. Yeah,

they, they, they, they use some of them. And we never did that. We had no occasion, for the simple reason it was, we had a repertoire that we could play all night and never play the same thing over. When you play 32 dances at a ball in six hours, and you don't play no repeats, you ain't, you don't need no hymns. Did Jacqueline ever tell you about the day we put on the German band over the river? No, I didn't. Did you ever hear the Logical Point? Yes, I have heard of that. Did you ever hear it, Parker? No. We went over there to play a parade for the Logical Point in Algiers. So Martin Kirch, Joe Castro, my brother Lance, and myself, Martin says, what you say if we play the German band? So we was waiting for the parade to start, you know. So, all right, we walked about a block away from where the band was congregated, got out on the corner and played German band music, you know. And by the time they had her on and put the peak in the back, let's play German music like sailor hats. You know, Martin Kirch went around with his hat, you know, he was going to start collecting. Don't you know, I believe it again, that fella money? And when the people went to get money, they said, now, we just do it after fun. Well, Papa laying like they had a duck. And he didn't have a duck. That's the kind of fun we used to have. Martin Kirch, he told him, he says, spots, he didn't call them that, he called them something else. He says, if you ever come around with anything like that, he says, there ain't gonna be enough of you left, he says, to feed the fish. Oh, what's the matter with Jewish, he says. Don't put nothing like that off. We was a German band calling it tuba, trombone, clarinet. The German band used to go around at that particular time, see? and we had them down pat. Boy, I can see that, as good as if it happened last night. Boy, it was Papa Lane mad. See, man, he was burnt up. He called Martin everything that he could think of under the sun. He told him he was gonna do him too. Boy, Martin says, you gotta have a little fun, you can't have no fun with you. But Martin had his hat and then he was going around in God on. Everybody was standing out, you know, who was standing at the corner playing German music. He got up with his hat. People were gonna put something in there. They said, no, we're just doing that for fun.
